title: Collected Stories

vibeProfile.oneLine: Everyday life tilted into calm, inescapable nightmare.

summary: Here is the writer whose name became an adjective. Kafka's stories, from the notorious Metamorphosis, in which a man wakes as a monstrous insect, to A Hunger Artist and In the Penal Colony, turn everyday logic slightly, calmly wrong, until ordinary life reveals itself as a nightmare of guilt, authority and inexplicable rules. The tone is deadpan, even funny, which makes the dread worse. Read together, they map a whole modern condition: the individual small and baffled before systems that never explain themselves.
whyReadIt: The source of everything we call Kafkaesque. Short, strange and unforgettable, and funnier than you expect once you catch the deadpan.

funFacts.text: Kafka asked his friend Max Brod to burn all his manuscripts after his death; Brod published them instead.
